title: a `neural_block` descriptor whose `output_width` exceeds its `state_width` is rejected
why: Fixture content is row01's golden with `output_width` raised from 3 to 7,
`state_width` left at its golden value of 6 — the ONLY thing that can make
it reject is the width lock under test (both values individually pass the
positive-integer check, so this is not that row).
This wire-checkable width lock: a block's output
payload is committed into state rows `[0, output_width)` of its own
per-block state vector, so `output_width` cannot exceed `state_width` —
this is checkable from the wire fields alone, with no in-process
resolution needed, which is why it is a SIDECAR-level check rather than
deferred to NE1's in-process signature-match relation.
The check runs AFTER the positive-integer loop (both fields must
individually be valid positive integers before the relational check
between them is meaningful) and after the requiredness loop (both fields
must be present at all) — this fixture's golden-derived content passes
both of those, so it reaches exactly the check under test.
